# Oh My Cassette

The `cassette` MCP server is a local bridge to the Cassette video editor. Its editing tools come
from the Cassette MCP service and change as Cassette evolves, so this skill deliberately names none
of them. **The server's instructions and each tool's description are the source of truth**: read
them, and when they disagree with anything you remember, they win.

## Rules that hold for every version

1. **Follow the server.** Which tool to call, in what order, and how to route on a result are in the
   server instructions and the tool descriptions. Route on typed fields such as `status`, never on
   prose.
2. **Relay the user's words.** When a tool takes the user's editing request, pass it exactly as the
   user wrote it: no rewriting, summarizing, translating, or expanding. The Cassette agent reads the
   project media itself.
3. **Ground every claim in a tool result.** What is on the timeline, which version it is, and where
   the editor link points come from the latest result, not from memory.
4. **Render only when asked.** Export or render only when the user asks to export, render, download,
   or finish.
5. **Say where the media goes.** When the user has not asked for Cassette by name in this
   conversation, tell them before the first upload that the files they named go to the Cassette
   service for editing, and go on once they agree.

## Local files

- Pass file paths as the user gave them, absolute or relative to the workspace. The bridge prepares
  and uploads them and hands Cassette references in their place.
- Only files the user named or that sit in the workspace. Never search the filesystem for media.
- Files outside the workspace are refused unless the user adds their directory to
  `CASSETTE_ALLOWED_ROOTS`. Only video, audio, and image files upload.
- Video is transcoded on this machine with ffmpeg before it uploads, and audio or images Cassette
  does not take as they are get converted. Long footage can take minutes.
- Exported files are downloaded into `cassette-exports/` in the workspace. Use the local path the
  result gives you; never invent one. When the result says a file is still downloading, the download
  goes on in the background and the file appears where the result says: tell the user that, and do not
  export again to get it.

## Long waits

Long work never fails just for taking long. A tool waits a bounded time and then returns a normal,
non-error result that says the work is still going:

- **`status: "preparing"`** comes from the bridge: the local files are still being prepared or
  uploaded, and that work continues in the background. Tell the user the progress it reports, then
  call the same tool again with exactly the same arguments to keep waiting; it picks up the same
  work instead of starting over. Never keep calling for longer than the user is willing to wait:
  ask before you continue a long wait.
- **`running`, `processing` and similar statuses** come from Cassette. How to continue (usually the
  same tool with the id the result returns) is in the server instructions and the tool description.
- Cancelling a call only stops waiting; the work goes on. Stop the work itself only when the user
  asks, with the tool the server provides for that.

## When the bridge itself reports a problem

Errors whose code starts with `bridge.` come from the local bridge, not from Cassette. Any other
error code is Cassette's own: follow its message and the tool description.

| Code | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `bridge.backend_unreachable` | A tool that names its request in an argument has already been sent again by the bridge while the call's wait lasted. If the message says the connection broke during the call, the work may still be running: call the same tool again with the same arguments to pick it up. If it says Cassette did not take the call, retry after `retry_after_seconds` when the error gives it. Otherwise call `cassette_bridge_status` once, tell the user the service is not reachable and at which URL, and retry only after it reports connected. |
| `bridge.rate_limited` | Cassette is taking too many requests and did not run the call. Wait `retry_after_seconds` (from the error), then call the same tool again with the same arguments; do not retry sooner. |
| `bridge.forbidden` | This account or grant cannot access Cassette. Ask the user to check that they signed in with the account of their projects. Do not repeatedly trigger login. |
| `bridge.auth_unavailable` | Online authentication or secure credential storage is unavailable. Tell the user to restore the connection or unlock the system keyring, then retry. |
| `bridge.unauthorized` | The service refused the token. Tell the user to run `oh-my-cassette login`. The browser handles email verification and consent. Restart the MCP host only if it cannot refresh tools. Do not repeatedly trigger login. |
| `bridge.upgrade_required` | Tell the user to update the oh-my-cassette version their MCP host runs (the message links the steps: bump the `oh-my-cassette==` pin, or update the plugin). Do not retry. |
| `bridge.protocol_unsupported` | The service at that URL is too old for this plugin (it does not speak MCP 2026-07-28). Tell the user the Cassette service must be updated. Do not retry. |
| `bridge.file_not_found` | Ask the user for the correct path. |
| `bridge.file_outside_workspace` | Ask the user to copy the file into the workspace, or to add its directory to `CASSETTE_ALLOWED_ROOTS`. When the message says the host started the bridge in a folder too wide to read from (the whole disk or the home folder), ask them to set `CASSETTE_WORKSPACE` to the project folder. |
| `bridge.file_type_rejected` | Tell the user which types this tool accepts (the message lists them). |
| `bridge.file_too_large` | Tell the user about the size limit (`CASSETTE_MAX_UPLOAD_MB`). |
| `bridge.ffmpeg_unavailable` | Video needs ffmpeg on this machine. Relay the install hint from the message, or ask the user to set `CASSETTE_FFMPEG` and `CASSETTE_FFPROBE`. Do not retry until it is installed. |
| `bridge.prepare_failed` | ffmpeg could not read or convert the file. Tell the user which file failed and what the message says; do not retry the same file unchanged. |
| `bridge.upload_failed` | Retry once, then report it. |
| `bridge.invalid_argument` | Fix the arguments: file parameters take a path or a list of paths. |
| `bridge.contract_violation` | A Cassette service bug. Report it to the user as is; do not retry. |

A failed export download (`bridge.download_failed`) does not fail the call: the result says so and
keeps the original URL, which you can give the user.

## When only `cassette_bridge_status` is listed

The service is offline, refused the sign-in, or needs a newer plugin. Call `cassette_bridge_status`
once and tell the user what it reports (URL, `error_code` and reason). Do not poll it. When the
service comes back, its tools appear by themselves; if this host does not refresh tool lists, ask
the user to restart the MCP server.

Oh My Cassette

Edit video by talking to the Cassette agent from Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Hermes.
A small MCP bridge, installed from PyPI. The editing tools come from the Cassette MCP service, so they stay current without a plugin update.

**One real Claude Code session, with every prompt shown as it was typed.** Five 4K travel films (10½ minutes of footage) and a song go in, a two-sentence brief and a one-line revision go to the Cassette agent word for word, and a 30-second 1080p MP4 lands in `cassette-exports/`. Waits are fast-forwarded: in real time the import took 4½ minutes, the first cut 9½, the revision 3½ and the export 1. > *Cut a 30-second teaser for Turkey from these five films, on the beat of Pamgaea.mp3. Open on a hot-air balloon > lighting up at dawn in Cappadocia, travel from the ancient ruins to the sea, name each place when it first appears, > and end on the misty lake with the title TURKEY.* > > *The ruins part drags. Keep only the two best Ephesus shots, and put the camel right after the balloons.*


Watch the teaser it made (MP4, 30 s, with sound). Footage and music credits are below.

## Install in 30 seconds You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (it fetches Python and the package on first start) and, to import video into a cloud project, [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html). **1. Add Oh My Cassette to your agent.** ```bash # Claude Code claude plugin marketplace add Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette claude plugin install oh-my-cassette@cassette-editor ``` ```bash # Codex codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette.git codex plugin add oh-my-cassette@cassette-editor ``` ```bash # Hermes hermes mcp add cassette --command uvx --args oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 ``` For OpenCode or any other MCP host, see [Install](#install) below. **2. Sign in**, whichever host you use: ```bash uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 login ``` Your browser asks for the code Cassette emails you. Then restart your agent if it cannot refresh its tool list, and say: > *Start a new Cassette project and import the clips in ./footage, then cut a 30-second travel video with a title at the start.* ## Projects and retention A new project lives in the cloud unless you place it on one of your Macs; when your account has a Mac running Cassette for Mac, the service asks which you want. - **A cloud project** is deleted with its media after three idle days. Every use pushes that back, and each answer says when it is due (`retention_expires_at`). Exported files are already on your machine in `cassette-exports/` and stay there. - **A project held by Cassette for Mac** is kept. The bridge can open, edit, import into and export it while that Mac is online. When the bridge runs on that Mac, the app reads each file where it is and nothing uploads; from any other machine each file uploads unchanged, with its embedded metadata, and the cloud copy is deleted once the Mac has it. [docs/privacy.md](https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette/blob/main/docs/privacy.md) has the details. ## Overview Oh My Cassette connects your coding agent to the Cassette editing agent. It is a local stdio MCP server that relays to the Cassette MCP service (`CASSETTE_MCP_URL`), which in turn calls the Cassette backend: ```text Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Hermes ──stdio──▶ oh-my-cassette ──HTTP──▶ Cassette MCP service ──▶ Cassette backend ``` - **The tools are the service's.** Whatever it lists (projects, editing turns, questions, undo, export) is what your agent sees, with the service's own descriptions and workflow instructions. When Cassette changes, the tools change with it; the plugin does not need a release. - **The bridge adds only what needs your machine.** Local files named in a call are sent first (only from the workspace, media types only). For a cloud project they are prepared here: video is transcoded with ffmpeg into the renditions the service declares, and audio or images the service cannot take as they are get converted. For a project a Mac holds they go as they are (see [Projects and retention](#projects-and-retention)). Each file uploads while the next one is prepared, in parts, four transfers at a time; a file whose upload was interrupted picks up its earlier import when you import it again. Exported files are downloaded into `cassette-exports/`. The workspace identity travels with each call so the service can remember a project per directory. - **Long work never times out the host.** Every call waits a bounded time; slow local preparation answers `preparing` and keeps going in the background, and the next identical call picks it up. An export download that outlasts the wait goes on in the background too, and the answer says where the file will appear. - **It survives deploys.** It reconnects on its own, retries a call that carries a request id when the connection drops or the service turns it away, resumes interrupted downloads, reports `bridge.*` errors with a `retryable` flag (and `retry_after_seconds` when the service said when), and, while the service is unreachable or refuses the token, lists a single `cassette_bridge_status` tool that says why. The rules between the plugin and the service are defined in [`src/oh_my_cassette/contract.py`](https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette/blob/main/src/oh_my_cassette/contract.py); `oh-my-cassette check` verifies a service against them. ## Requirements - An invited Cassette account. While the service is unreachable or refuses your sign-in, the only tool listed is `cassette_bridge_status`, which says why. - [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) 0.5 or newer. `uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0` resolves Python 3.11 or newer by itself. - [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) (with ffprobe) to import video into a cloud project: `brew install ffmpeg`, `sudo apt install ffmpeg` or `winget install ffmpeg`. Video is transcoded on your machine before it uploads, and a build with `zscale` also tone-maps HDR footage properly. A project held by Cassette for Mac does not need it. The service declares which file types each tool accepts and how they are prepared; the bridge sends only video, audio and images unless you set `CASSETTE_UPLOAD_ANY_TYPE`. ## Configuration Sign in once with `oh-my-cassette login`, using the Cassette account that holds your projects; the browser asks for the emailed code and your consent. One sign-in reaches every project of the account, whether it was made on the web or in Cassette for Mac. `login`, `status` and `logout` keep the credentials in your operating-system keyring, so no token needs to be copied. The environment variables below are optional overrides. | Variable | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `CASSETTE_MCP_URL` | the saved connection, otherwise `https://mcp.trycassette.online/mcp` | Explicit MCP endpoint override. | | `CASSETTE_AUTH_TOKEN` | unset | Advanced bearer-token override. Normally use `login`; the same account, scope and resource checks apply. Never place it in shared configuration. | | `CASSETTE_WORKSPACE` | the directory the host starts the server in | Where relative paths resolve, where local files may come from, and the directory the service may remember a project for. A host that starts the server in the whole disk or your home folder gives it no files to read until you set this, or `CASSETTE_ALLOWED_ROOTS`. | | `CASSETTE_ALLOWED_ROOTS` | unset | Extra directories local files may come from (`:`-separated; `;` on Windows). | | `CASSETTE_DOWNLOAD_DIR` | `/cassette-exports` | Where exported files are saved. The default must stay inside the workspace: a `cassette-exports` symlink leading elsewhere is refused. | | `CASSETTE_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` / `CASSETTE_MAX_DOWNLOAD_MB` | `4096` / `16384` | Size limits per file. | | `CASSETTE_UPLOAD_ANY_TYPE` | off | Allow non-media uploads when a tool accepts them. | | `CASSETTE_LOCAL_WAIT_SEC` | `240` | How long one call waits for local preparation and upload before it answers `preparing`. | | `CASSETTE_FFMPEG` / `CASSETTE_FFPROBE` | from `PATH` | The ffmpeg and ffprobe programs used to prepare local media. | | `CASSETTE_TEMP_DIR` | the system temp directory | Where each upload makes its own private directory (`oh-my-cassette-job-*`) for prepared files until they are uploaded. | | `CASSETTE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SEC` | `10` | How long to wait for the service when connecting. | | `CASSETTE_MCP_HOST` | unset | The host name sent to the service when the host does not identify itself. | | `CASSETTE_AUTH_DIRECTORY` | `~/.config/oh-my-cassette` | Where the saved connection's settings are kept (the token and your own OpenAI key stay in the keyring). | | `OH_MY_CASSETTE_LOG` | `WARNING` | Log level on stderr. | ### Your own OpenAI key An account can pay for its Cassette agent turns with its own OpenAI key instead of Cassette's. Save it once, after `login`: ```bash uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 key set # prompts for the key (sk-…) without echoing it uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 key status # shows whether one is saved, and its fingerprint uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 key remove ``` The key stays in your operating-system keyring (service `oh-my-cassette.provider-key`), kept for the account you signed in with, and is never written to a file. The bridge sends it in the `x-cassette-provider-key` header on its requests to the Cassette MCP service only; the service hands it to Cassette, which holds it in memory while your turns need it and switches the account to its own key. `key remove` first has Cassette let go of the key it holds at once, then forgets it here; the account stays on its own key, so its turns wait for one until you set a key again. Switch back to Cassette's key in Cassette settings. A turn that waits for a key Cassette does not hold answers `needs_credential`; save the key and continue the turn. With `CASSETTE_AUTH_TOKEN` set, no key is sent. `status` shows the fingerprint Cassette shows: the first 8 hex digits of the key's SHA-256 and its last four characters. ## Install ### Claude Code Plugin (recommended): the two commands at the top. The plugin uses the connection saved by `oh-my-cassette login` and starts `uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0` with a 10-minute tool timeout. Project scope without the plugin: copy [`.mcp.json`](https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette/blob/main/.mcp.json) into your project, or run: ```bash claude mcp add --transport stdio cassette -- uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 ``` The skill lives in [`skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette/blob/main/skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md) and ships with the plugin. ### Codex Plugin: the two commands at the top ([`.codex-plugin/plugin.json`](https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette/blob/main/.codex-plugin/plugin.json) declares the server inline with `tool_timeout_sec: 600` and passes the `CASSETTE_*` variables through from your shell). Or add the server directly: ```bash codex mcp add cassette -- uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 ``` ### OpenCode Add to `opencode.json` (project or `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`): ```json { "mcp": { "cassette": { "type": "local", "command": ["uvx", "oh-my-cassette==0.7.0"], "timeout": 600000 } } } ``` Then copy the skill so OpenCode loads it: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/skills/cassette-video-edit curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette/v0.7.0/skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md \ -o ~/.config/opencode/skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md ``` OpenCode has no MCP elicitation, which is fine: the editing agent's questions come back as ordinary tool results, and the service's tools say how to answer them. ### Hermes ```bash hermes mcp add cassette --command uvx --args oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 mkdir -p ~/.hermes/skills/cassette-video-edit curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette/v0.7.0/skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md \ -o ~/.hermes/skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md ``` Set `mcp_servers.cassette.timeout: 600` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` so a call's bounded waits fit. Hermes is a plain MCP host here: the 0.4 gateway/plugin layer is gone. ### Any other MCP host Command `uvx`, args `["oh-my-cassette==0.7.0"]`, stdio transport, a tool timeout of 10 minutes, and the environment variables above. No uv? `pipx run oh-my-cassette==0.7.0` works too. ## How a turn looks ```text you: Import intro.mp4 and beach.mov, then make a 20-second cut with the title "Kota Kinabalu". agent: (calls the service's import tool with ["intro.mp4", "beach.mov"]) bridge: transcodes both videos, uploads them, passes the service media references (calls the service's editing tool with your sentence, verbatim; progress streams while it runs) "Done. Added a 20 s cut from both clips with the title at the start. 服务列出什么（项目、剪辑对话、回答提问、撤销、导出），你的 agent 就看到什么， 描述和工作流说明也都来自服务。Cassette 改了，工具跟着变，插件不用发版。 - **bridge 只做必须在你电脑上做的事。** 调用里写到的本地文件会先发送出去（只限工作区内、只限媒体类型）。 云端项目的文件先在本机预处理：视频用 ffmpeg 转码成服务声明的各个产物，服务不直接接受的音频和图片先转换； # Contributing to Oh My Cassette

Thanks for helping. This repository is a single Python package (`src/oh_my_cassette`) that every host
runs the same way, plus one skill that is copied to two places. The package is a generic bridge to
the Cassette MCP service: it never names a backend tool, and everything the two sides agree on is in
`src/oh_my_cassette/contract.py`. Changes must keep that contract intact, or change `contract.py`,
`tests/reference_remote.py` and the Cassette MCP service together.

## Conventional commits

Release Please derives versions and changelog entries from commits on `main`:

- `feat: …` — user-visible feature;
- `fix: …` — bug fix;
- `feat!: …` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer — breaking change;
- `docs: …`, `ci: …`, `chore: …`, `test: …`, and `refactor: …` — no release bump by themselves
  (`release-please-config.json` hides them from the changelog).

PRs are squash-merged using the PR title, so the title must itself be a conventional commit line.
Branch from `main` and target `main`; a PR merges once the `ci-ok` check is green. The `release`
branch is frozen at 0.5.0 for 0.4 installs and takes no commits (see [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md)).

By contributing you agree that your contribution is licensed under the MIT License of this
repository.

## Development setup

```bash
uv sync --group dev          # creates .venv with the package, pytest, ruff, starlette, uvicorn
uv run pytest -q -rs         # reference service on loopback, no network
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format .
```

`ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` must be on PATH for `tests/test_prepare.py`, which runs the real ffmpeg; without
them that module is skipped.

Run the server from the checkout inside a host while you work:

```bash
claude mcp add cassette-dev -e OH_MY_CASSETTE_LOG=DEBUG -- uv run --directory "$PWD" oh-my-cassette
```

## Tests

- `tests/reference_remote.py` is an executable reference service for the contract (token, `prepare`,
  the upload handshake, downloads, bounded waits). The bridge tests drive the real bridge against it
  through a real MCP client; `tests/test_conformance.py` runs `oh-my-cassette check` against it and
  against broken variants.
- `tests/test_prepare.py` transcodes generated samples with the real ffmpeg and checks every rendition
  with ffprobe; `tests/test_local_jobs.py` covers the `preparing` status and attaching to running work.
- `tests/test_manifests.py` pins the version and the `uvx oh-my-cassette==X.Y.Z` pins across every
  manifest, checks the host timeouts and environment, and checks that both skill copies are identical,
  name no backend tool and cover every `bridge.*` error code.
- The live test is for maintainers: it runs against a Cassette MCP service and an invited account
  (production by default, or a local Cassette stack through `CASSETTE_MCP_URL`), and is skipped by
  default because it imports media and exports, which renders through the service's provider:

  ```bash
  uvx oh-my-cassette login                     # once, or set CASSETTE_AUTH_TOKEN
  RUN_CASSETTE_LIVE=1 uv run pytest tests/live -q -rs
  ```

CI runs lint and the suite on Linux only (Python 3.11, 3.13 and 3.14), builds the wheel and starts it
once with `uvx`; the `ci-ok` job sums them up. It installs no ffmpeg, whose package mirrors stalled its
runs, so `tests/test_prepare.py` runs only locally: run the whole suite with ffmpeg before a release. Keep it credential-free and
deterministic.

## Changing the contract

1. Change `src/oh_my_cassette/contract.py` and the Cassette MCP service together; v1 only grows by
   additions.
2. Teach `tests/reference_remote.py` the change and test it through the bridge.
3. Add a conformance check, with a broken variant, when a service could get it wrong.
4. A new `bridge.*` error code goes into both skill copies' error table
   (`skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md`).
5. Update `README.md` and `README.zh-cn.md` together.

## What not to commit

`.venv`, `cassette-exports/`, real tokens or passwords, media beyond the tiny fixtures in
`tests/fixtures/`, and service URLs that are not the local defaults.

# Installing Oh My Cassette (for AI agents)

Oh My Cassette is a stdio MCP bridge published on PyPI as `oh-my-cassette`. Hosts start it with
`uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0`; there is nothing to clone or build. It relays to the Cassette MCP
service at `CASSETTE_MCP_URL`, so the editing tools come from that service.

## Prerequisites

- `uv` on PATH (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/). It provides Python 3.11 or newer.
- `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` on PATH to import video (`brew install ffmpeg`, `sudo apt install ffmpeg`,
  `winget install ffmpeg`), or `CASSETTE_FFMPEG` / `CASSETTE_FFPROBE` set to them.
- An invited Cassette account. Sign in once with `uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 login` (the browser
  asks for an emailed code and consent; tokens go to the OS keyring). Check the service with
  `uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 check`: every line should be PASS.

## Claude Code

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette
claude plugin install oh-my-cassette@cassette-editor
```

Then sign in once (`uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 login`) if you have not. Or project scope:
`claude mcp add --transport stdio cassette -- uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0`.
Health check: `claude mcp list` shows `cassette: … - ✓ Connected`.

## Codex

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette.git
codex plugin add oh-my-cassette@cassette-editor
```

The plugin passes `CASSETTE_*` variables through from the shell. Or:
`codex mcp add cassette -- uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0`.

## OpenCode

Add the `mcp.cassette` block from `opencode.json` in this repository to the user's `opencode.json`,
then copy `skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md` to `~/.config/opencode/skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md`.

## Hermes

```bash
hermes mcp add cassette --command uvx --args oh-my-cassette==0.7.0

```

Copy `skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md` to `~/.hermes/skills/cassette-video-edit/SKILL.md` and set
`mcp_servers.cassette.timeout: 600` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.

## Tool timeout

Configure 600 seconds (600000 ms where the host counts milliseconds). Every call stays within it:
the bridge waits at most `CASSETTE_LOCAL_WAIT_SEC` (240) for local preparation and the service waits a
bounded time for its own work; longer work answers `preparing`, `running` or `processing` and continues
on the next call.

## Environment variables

`CASSETTE_MCP_URL` (optional endpoint override), `CASSETTE_AUTH_TOKEN` (advanced credential override), `CASSETTE_WORKSPACE` (default: the server's working directory), `CASSETTE_ALLOWED_ROOTS`,
`CASSETTE_DOWNLOAD_DIR`, `CASSETTE_MAX_UPLOAD_MB`, `CASSETTE_MAX_DOWNLOAD_MB`, `CASSETTE_UPLOAD_ANY_TYPE`,
`CASSETTE_LOCAL_WAIT_SEC`, `CASSETTE_FFMPEG`, `CASSETTE_FFPROBE`, `CASSETTE_TEMP_DIR`,
`CASSETTE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SEC`, `CASSETTE_MCP_HOST`, `CASSETTE_AUTH_DIRECTORY`, `OH_MY_CASSETTE_LOG`.
See README.md for defaults.

## Verify

`uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 --version` prints `oh-my-cassette` and the version you pinned. In the host, the
tool list should show the service's tools. If it shows only `cassette_bridge_status`, call it: it reports the
endpoint URL, an `error_code` (`bridge.backend_unreachable`, `bridge.unauthorized`, `bridge.forbidden`,
`bridge.auth_unavailable`, `bridge.protocol_unsupported` or `bridge.upgrade_required`) and the reason.

## Uninstalling

Sign out first with `uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 logout` (it revokes the grant and deletes the keyring
entry), then remove the server from the host config (`claude plugin uninstall oh-my-cassette@cassette-editor`,
`codex plugin remove oh-my-cassette`, delete the `opencode.json` block, `hermes mcp remove cassette`),
delete `~/.config/oh-my-cassette` (connection metadata, no token) and run `uv cache clean oh-my-cassette`.
Exported files stay in `cassette-exports/`.

# Oh My Cassette

> Oh My Cassette is an open-source MCP server (PyPI: `oh-my-cassette`) that lets Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Hermes drive the Cassette video editor: import local media, send the user's editing requests to the Cassette agent one turn at a time, read the versioned timeline back, undo/redo, and export.

Hosts start it with `uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0`. It is a generic bridge to the Cassette MCP service (`CASSETTE_MCP_URL`, Streamable HTTP, bearer token): the editing tools, their descriptions and the workflow instructions come from that service. The bridge adds only what needs the user's machine: it transcodes local video with ffmpeg and uploads local files before a call, downloads exported files after one, and answers a typed `preparing` status while local work continues in the background. MIT licensed.

# Releasing Oh My Cassette

Releases are automated with [Release Please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please) and
published to PyPI with trusted publishing. Nothing is uploaded by hand, and nothing publishes
without a maintainer's approval.

## What a release changes

The standing release PR (`release-type: python`) bumps, in one commit:

- `pyproject.toml` `version` and `src/oh_my_cassette/__init__.py` (`x-release-please-version` marker);
- `.release-please-manifest.json` and `CHANGELOG.md`;
- the bare version fields in `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`,
  `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `server.json` (`extra-files` in `release-please-config.json`).

Release Please cannot rewrite strings inside other text, so `release-please.yml` then runs a sed on
the release PR branch and pushes a `chore: pin host manifests and docs to X.Y.Z` commit that moves:

- the `oh-my-cassette==X.Y.Z` pins in `.mcp.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `opencode.json`, both
  READMEs, `llms.txt`, `llms-install.md`, `SUPPORT.md`, `SECURITY.md` and `docs/`;
- the `"ref": "vX.Y.Z"` of both plugin marketplaces (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`,
  `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`), and the skill download URLs in both READMEs, to the tag the
  release will create.

A pull request or push made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no workflow, so `release-please.yml` also
dispatches `ci.yml` on the release PR branch. That run produces the `ci-ok` check `main` requires, and
`tests/test_manifests.py` in it fails if any version, pin or tag reference disagrees.

Merging the release PR creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag and the GitHub Release. `release-please.yml` then:

1. checks out the tag and verifies that it pins its own version and that both marketplaces name it;
2. dispatches `publish-pypi.yml` on the tag. The run waits in the `pypi` environment for a
   maintainer's approval (**Actions → the run → Review deployments**); after it, `uv build`, a check
   that the tag equals the package version, publishing the wheel and sdist with OIDC (no API token),
   and once PyPI serves the version, publishing `server.json` to the MCP registry
   (`mcp-publisher login github-oidc`, the binary checked against its release checksum; ownership is
   proven by the `mcp-name: io.github.Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette` marker in the README that PyPI
   shows).

| Channel | Runtime comes from | Manifests come from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code plugin, Codex plugin | PyPI (`uvx oh-my-cassette==X.Y.Z`, pinned in the manifests) | the `vX.Y.Z` tag the marketplace entries on `main` name |

Tags cannot be moved or deleted (a ruleset on `refs/tags/v*`), so what a plugin install fetches is

The `release` branch is frozen at 0.5.0 and takes no commits (a ruleset blocks updates and
deletion). It exists for 0.4 installs: their plugin marketplaces pinned `ref: release`, and their

PyPI lists `Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette`, workflow `publish-pypi.yml`, environment `pypi` as the

- deploys only from tags matching `v*`.

# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report vulnerabilities privately through [GitHub private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette/security/advisories/new), not a public issue. We acknowledge a report within three working days and coordinate the fix and its disclosure with you.

## Supported versions

| Version | Supported |
| --- | --- |
| 0.5.x (PyPI) | Yes: fixes ship in the latest 0.5 release |
| 0.4.x and earlier (git installs) | No: upgrade to 0.5 |

## Trust boundaries

Everything this repository ships runs on the user's machine. Every host (Claude Code, Codex,
OpenCode, Hermes) launches `uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0` as a local stdio child process. The bridge
opens no port; only an explicit `login` briefly binds an ephemeral loopback callback for the browser
sign-in.

The Cassette MCP service configured with `CASSETTE_MCP_URL` (and the backend behind it) is a
separate service that receives the access token, media, editing requests, project state and render
requests. Do not treat the local process and the service as the same thing: a report about
rendering, storage, or account handling belongs to Cassette, not here.

The service decides which tools exist and what their descriptions, instructions and results say;
the bridge passes that text to the host's agent unchanged, so the agent follows the service's
guidance as it would a tool's. What the bridge reads, writes and contacts is decided locally,
whatever the service says:

- Local files come only from the workspace or `CASSETTE_ALLOWED_ROOTS`, and only media types unless
  the user sets `CASSETTE_UPLOAD_ANY_TYPE`; a tool can narrow that set but never widen it. A host
  that starts the bridge in the whole disk or the home folder gives it no workspace to read from.
  A picture or a sound uploaded unchanged must begin like one.
- Media preparation takes only encodings the bridge knows (codec, profile, preset, pixel format,
  container), so a declaration cannot add ffmpeg filters or options. ffmpeg reads its input as a
  local file only.
- Uploads and downloads, redirects included, go only to the service's own origin or to HTTPS hosts
  whose every address is public, so the URLs the service hands out cannot reach the machine's own
  network. A PUT never carries a host, cookie, proxy or connection header the service names.
- Downloads are written only into the download directory, which stays inside the workspace unless
  `CASSETTE_DOWNLOAD_DIR` names another. Names are sanitized, an existing file or symlink is never
  overwritten or written through, and the size and SHA-256 are checked when the service declares them.

## Credentials and local state

- The bearer token (the OAuth access token, or `CASSETTE_AUTH_TOKEN`) is sent to the MCP service,
  and to upload and download URLs only when they have the same origin as the service; presigned
  URLs on other origins get no credential, and a redirect to another origin drops it. A saved
  sign-in is bound to the endpoint it was made for, so a `CASSETTE_MCP_URL` override never receives
  it. The service answers HTTP 401 without a valid token, reported as `bridge.unauthorized`.
- OAuth access and refresh tokens live only in the OS keyring (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential
  Vault, or Linux Secret Service). A file lock serializes refresh across hosts. Public connection
  metadata lives in `~/.config/oh-my-cassette` (mode 0700); it contains no token. `logout` revokes
  the grant before deleting credentials.
- Prepared media lives in a private `oh-my-cassette-job-*` directory (mode 0700) under
  `CASSETTE_TEMP_DIR` (default: the system temporary directory) only until it is uploaded.
- ffmpeg and ffprobe run as local subprocesses with argument lists, never through a shell, and are
  looked up on `PATH`, never in the working directory.

## Agent skill

The bundled skill (`skills/cassette-video-edit`) lets an agent offer Cassette for a video-editing
request even when the user does not name it. Before the first upload in a conversation where the
user did not ask for Cassette, it tells the user that the named files go to the Cassette service.

# Support

## What this repository is

Oh My Cassette is the **client**: a local MCP server (PyPI `oh-my-cassette`) plus a skill. It
imports your media, relays your editing requests to the Cassette agent one turn at a time, reads the
timeline back, and downloads exports.

The **editing engine is the Cassette backend** ([Cassette](https://trycassette.online)). It runs the
agent that watches your footage, edits the timeline and renders. It is a separate service and is not
in this repository.

That split decides where a given problem can be solved, so it is worth knowing before you file.

The editing service is a separate product. This plugin exists so the workflow is usable — and
inspectable — from real agents today. Everything on the client side is MIT licensed and open to
contribution; questions about the service's own roadmap or availability are best asked in
Discussions, where we can answer them directly.

Oh My Cassette connects your coding agent — [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code),
[Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex), [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) or
[Hermes Agent](https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent) — to the Cassette editing agent. It is a
local stdio MCP server that relays to the Cassette MCP service: your agent passes your words through,
Cassette edits, and the finished video lands in `cassette-exports/`.

## Install

```bash
# Claude Code
claude plugin marketplace add Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette
claude plugin install oh-my-cassette@cassette-editor
```

```bash
# Codex
codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette.git
codex plugin add oh-my-cassette@cassette-editor
```

Then sign in once with `uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 login`. Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/),
`ffmpeg` for video, and an invited [Cassette](https://trycassette.online) account. Other hosts and
every option are in the [README](https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette#readme).

# Privacy notice — Oh My Cassette plugin

_Last reviewed: 2026-10-21, for 0.5.0. This file is versioned; `git log docs/privacy.md` is the change history._

This notice covers the **Oh My Cassette plugin** — the local MCP bridge and the skill in
[this repository](https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette).

[Cassette](https://trycassette.online) is a **separate hosted service** that does the editing and
rendering. This notice does not speak for it. Anything you send there is governed by your agreement
with Cassette.

## The short version

The bridge runs on your machine as a stdio child of your agent and opens no port (`login` briefly
binds a loopback callback for the browser sign-in). It contains **no telemetry, no analytics, no
crash reporting and no update check** — nothing reports back to this project. It talks to the
Cassette MCP endpoint (`https://mcp.trycassette.online/mcp` unless you set `CASSETTE_MCP_URL`), to
the sign-in service that endpoint names, and to the upload and download URLs the endpoint hands it
(the endpoint's own origin, or public HTTPS hosts only).

## What leaves your machine

| What | To | When |
|---|---|---|
| An OAuth access token, as a bearer token | the service | every call to the service, and to upload or download URLs on the service's own origin; presigned URLs on other origins get no credential |
| The refresh token, and the grant to revoke | the sign-in service | when an expiring access token is renewed, and on `logout` |
| `oh-my-cassette/<version>` as the User-Agent | the service | every request |
| Your editing requests and answers, as your agent passes them | the service | every tool call your agent makes |
| The workspace: an opaque identifier for its directory and the directory's name (not its path) | the service | every tool call |
| The host's name and version (e.g. Claude Code 2.x), as the host reports it or `CASSETTE_MCP_HOST` sets it | the service | every tool call |
| For each file a call names: its name, its path relative to the workspace and its absolute path, its size and SHA-256, and its type | the service | when a tool call names it |
| The files themselves: prepared for a cloud project, as they are for a project a Mac elsewhere holds | the upload URLs the service hands out | only when a tool call names them; nothing uploads on startup, in the background or on a schedule |

Before upload, video is transcoded on your machine with ffmpeg into the renditions the service
declares, which drops the source's metadata (camera, location, timestamps). Audio and images the
service takes as they are upload **unchanged, with their embedded metadata** — for example a photo's
EXIF GPS position or a song's ID3 tags; ones it does not take as they are get converted. Files come
only from the workspace or `CASSETTE_ALLOWED_ROOTS`, and only media types unless you set
`CASSETTE_UPLOAD_ANY_TYPE`.

A project made in Cassette for Mac takes its media only into that Mac's library, so its files are not
prepared here. When the bridge runs on that Mac, the app reads each file from its absolute path and
nothing uploads. From any other machine each file uploads **unchanged, with its embedded metadata**,
and Cassette deletes the cloud copy once the Mac has it.

Sign-in happens in your browser on Cassette's own pages (an emailed code and a consent screen); the
bridge never sees a password.

## What stays on your machine

- **Tokens.** OAuth access and refresh tokens live only in the operating-system keyring (macOS
  Keychain, Windows Credential Vault or Linux Secret Service).
- **Connection metadata.** The endpoint and account you signed in to, in `~/.config/oh-my-cassette`.
  It contains no token.
- **Prepared media.** Transcoded files sit in a private directory under `CASSETTE_TEMP_DIR`
  (default: the system temporary directory) only until they are uploaded.
- **Exports.** Downloaded videos are saved in `cassette-exports/` in your workspace (or
  `CASSETTE_DOWNLOAD_DIR`) and stay there.

## What Cassette keeps

A project the bridge starts is a cloud project unless you place it on one of your Macs. Cassette deletes it, with its media, after three idle
days; every use pushes that back, and each answer says when it is due (`retention_expires_at`). A
project made in Cassette for Mac stays on that Mac and is kept. For anything else Cassette stores,
ask Cassette.

## Your controls

| You want to | Do this |
|---|---|
| Limit what can be read | Keep media in the workspace, or grant narrow `CASSETTE_ALLOWED_ROOTS` — never your whole home directory |
| Sign this machine out | `uvx oh-my-cassette==0.7.0 logout` — revokes the grant, then deletes the keyring entry |
| Remove everything local | Sign out, delete `~/.config/oh-my-cassette`, and uninstall the plugin |
| Delete a cloud project now | Delete it in Cassette, or leave it idle for three days |

## Reporting

Report a privacy or security problem privately through
[GitHub private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette/security/advisories/new),
not a public issue. [`SECURITY.md`](https://github.com/Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
documents the trust boundaries in more detail.
